findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee on the cook line handle a baked potato with bare hands. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding glove use and hand washing. Ensure ready-to-eat foods are always handled with clean, gloved hands.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed no sanitizer available on the cook-line during food service. The PIC was informed and sanitizer was prepared, measuring 100ppm chlorine. This violation is considered corrected-on-site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to have no valid certified food protection manager. The PIC’s CFPM expired on 2/11/2026. The PIC was informed and plans to schedule the course and exam.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Chicken was stored directly above fish in the bottom of the prep cooler on the cook line.
2. Raw beef was stored directly above strawberries in the bottom of the prep cooler on the cook line. 
3. Inspector observed chicken stored directly above beef in the walk-in cooler

The PIC was informed of these violations and storage order was corrected. Ensure all staff are following proper storage order practices in the coolers to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed that PIC’s allergen certification is expired. PIC was aware that certification is expired, and will schedule to renew. Ensure compliance by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler. These storage order violations were also observed in the previous spot check and last routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw beef must be stored above raw chicken due to the beef’s lower minimum cooking temperature. All storage order violations were corrected on site. A spot check will be conducted in the near future to ensure storage order guidelines are being followed. Ensure staff are educated on the proper order of storage for raw meats.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Repeat
Observed raw chicken stored above raw fish as well as raw beef stored over cottage cheese. These are the same storage order violations observed during the previous routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw fish must be stored above raw chicken due to fish’s lower cook temperature. Any raw meat must be stored below ready-to-eat (RTE) foods such as dairy products and sauces. All storage order violations were corrected on-site. Storage order will be spot-checked during the scheduled follow-up on 3/12/25.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat 
Observed multiple items to be missing date marking (deli meats in prep cooler, cut vegetables and cooked meat in walk-in cooler). PIC was informed that any time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food stored in refrigeration for more than 24 hours needs to be properly date-marked and discarded after 7 days of retention. PIC placed labels on all required foods in prep cooler and walk-in during spot check. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days (3/12/2025) to ensure that proper date marking is being followed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed a can of green beans being heated on a gas cook stove in its original packaging. Informed PIC that the can the green beans are packaged in is not a proper cooking utensil. The green beans were transferred to an appropriate vessel (metal pan) to complete its cooking. Violation is considered corrected on site.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an individual fail to use a barrier to turn off hand-sink faucet. Advised PIC to review proper handwashing with staff. A barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to prevent cross-contamination prior to handling food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following storage order violations:
1. Cooked turkey stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
2. Cooked noodles stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
3. Fish stored under raw chicken and raw beef in prep cooler
4. Raw hamburger stored over ready-to-eat feta cheese in prep cooler

Advised PIC of proper storage order practices. Ready-to-eat foods must always be stored above raw foods and raw foods must be stored according to their minimum cooking temperatures. PIC corrected all storage order issues in coolers. A handout was also provided explaining proper storage order in more detail. The inspector will spot check for storage order during the scheduled follow-up.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a chlorine concentration of 0ppm in the dishwasher in the ware-washing room. Informed PIC of issue. He tried to correct the sanitizer concentration, but was unsuccessful. PIC has scheduled maintenance on the dish machine and has been informed to use sanitizer in his triple sink until the dishwasher is fixed. A follow-up to check the dishwasher’s function is scheduled for 3/10/25. Ensure that the dishwasher has proper sanitizer concentration or a sanitizing step in the triple sink is used for all food contact equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
This is a repeat violation. 

Observed portioned, sliced deli meat in prep cooler to not be date marked. PIC confirmed that deli meat has been in the cooler for 3-4 days. Informed PIC that any time/temperature control for safety (TCS), ready-to-eat foods stored in refrigeration must be marked with the date in which the item was opened or thawed. The food items must be discarded after 7 days from the marked date. PIC added labels to the deli meat and agreed to mark them moving forward.

findings.comment: Observed scoop for ice machine to be stored on top of machine. The top of the machine was soiled with dust and debris. Ensure the ice scoop is stored on a clean surface before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed employee touch RTE bun with bare hands. Bun was discarded. Discussed proper food handling and glove use with PIC and employee.

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed containers of cooked chicken and cooked meatloaf in walk-in-cooler to not have a date mark. Per PIC, items were prepared the previous day (6/19/24). Items were marked with proper date during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution available for use on cook line during food preparation. Sanitizer bucket was made during inspection and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.16: Observed wet mop head to be stored head down in mop bucket. Mop was hung properly during inspection. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
